**Question:** Should `reset-token` print only the token, or also tell the administrator when it expires so they can pass the deadline on to the user? (FR-032)

Why it matters: the administrator has to tell the user how long they have, and if the tool prints a second line, anything that captures the token from standard output has to know to read just the first line.

**Recommended:** Option A — The administrator either typed the `--ttl` they wanted or is using the documented 900-second default, so an extra line tells them something they already know, while a single-line output stays trivially usable from a script or a copy-paste. Keeping standard output to exactly the token also preserves the existing convention that these commands print one short line and nothing more.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Standard output is exactly the token on one line and nothing else. (current spec) |
| B | Standard output is the token on the first line, then a second line stating the lifetime or the expiry moment. |
| C | The token on standard output; the lifetime or expiry as an informational line on standard error, leaving standard output machine-clean. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
